questions.question_text: When assessing an angry and agitated patient, which of the following measures is advised?

options.text: Avoid panic alarms because this irritates the patient
Consider taking notes after the assessment has been completed
Let the patient sit between interviewer and the door
See the patient alone to allow disclosures of sensitive information
Stay as close as possible to the patient so that he or she feels secure

correct_answer.text: Consider taking notes after the assessment has been completed

correct_answers.text: Consider taking notes after the assessment has been completed

questions.explanation: When seeing an angry or agitated patient, it is advisable to consider taking notes after the assessment has been completed.

questions.question_text: When are closed questions most useful during a clinical assessment?

options.text: At the start of an interview
During the middle of unstructured interviews
To control an overtalkative patient during the assessment
When a chaperone presents during the assessment
When the patient accepts the situation and starts crying during the assessment

correct_answer.text: To control an overtalkative patient during the assessment

correct_answers.text: To control an overtalkative patient during the assessment

questions.explanation: Closed questions are useful to control an over-talkative patient during the assessment.

questions.question_text: If the psychiatrist asked a patient, 'Have you been feeling low in your mood recently?', what type of questioning style was used during the psychiatric interview?
questions.explanation: This is an example of a closed question that typically requires a yes or no answer.

questions.question_text: If the psychiatrist said to a patient 'You were not happy at that time?', what type of questioning style was used during the psychiatric interview?
questions.explanation: This question is leading, aiming for a specific response from the patient.

questions.question_text: If the psychiatrist asked a patient 'Tell me more about it?', what type of questioning style did he use during the psychiatric interview?
questions.explanation: This is an example of a directive question that prompts the patient to expand on their thoughts.

questions.question_text: Which lobe function is tested when the patient is asked to copy interlocking pentagons?

questions.question_text: In the mini-mental state examination (MMSE), what does the task of naming three objects test?
questions.explanation: The task tests registration by asking the patient to name three objects.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man had been drinking almost 35 units of alcohol a week for the last 7 years. He had numerous physical health and social difficulties. questions.question_text: Which of the following tests uses ambiguous stimuli to evaluate a person's patterns of thought, attitudes and observational capacity, and emotional responses?
questions.explanation: Rorschach's inkblot test is a projective test using ambiguous stimuli.

questions.question_text: A 72-year-old man was unable to draw interlocking polygons. Which of the following cerebral lobes is most likely to be affected?

questions.question_text: Which cognitive function is assessed by verbal frequency?

questions.question_text: A 29-year-old man was found wandering on the street with some memory loss after his 5-year-old son died suddenly. Which type of memory is most likely to be affected?
questions.explanation: This short scenario is about the fugue state, precipitated by his son’s death. Semantic memory is   affected in the fugue state

questions.question_text: A 28-year-old man presented with a few weeks history of elated mood, increased energy, persecutory ideas and auditory hallucinations. He thinks that he can save the world with his knowledge but aliens are interfering with his thoughts and control him. What is the most likely diagnosis? (AI chose Mania with psychosis)
questions.explanation: •	Schizoaffective disorder: schizophrenic and affective symptoms occur simultaneously or at   least within a few days of each other in the same episode of illness. The episode does not meet   the criteria for schizophrenia or affective disorder alone.  •	Delusional disorder: this can be safely ruled out because there is no history of schizophrenic   symptoms and no or occasional auditory hallucinations.  •	Mania with psychotic symptoms: there will be predominantly severe manic symptoms and   psychotic symptoms will follow the affective symptoms.  •	Paranoid schizophrenia: there will not have been simultaneous affective symptoms  •	Schizotypal disorder: this does not have any dominant or typical disturbance such as   schizophrenia or affective disorder. Its course is similar to a personality disorder. Also, the typical   features should be present for at least 2 years.

questions.question_text: A 21-year-old woman with an acute first psychotic episode was started on olanzapine 15 mg at night. After 10 days, she developed rigidity, pyrexia and autonomic instability. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation:
The following are differential diagnoses of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS):  •	Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: according to the DSM-IV, NMS is characterised by muscle   rigidity and an elevated temperature associated with the administration of an antipsychotic   medication. Two or more symptoms of autonomic instability need to be present, and blood   investigations should be instigated. There is an absence of infection, general medical condition   or substance use that may result in a similar condition. It is estimated to occur in 0.2–1% of   patients treated with dopamine-blocking agents. It is also known to occur in other neurological   disorders (e.g. Wilson’s disease, Parkinson’s disease treated with dopamine-blocking agents). It may also occur in patients treated with dopamine antagonists given for nausea (e.g. 
metoclopramide, prochlorperazine).
•	Encephalitis: this may present with a viral prodrome, meningeal signs, other neurological signs, 
seizures, and imaging and cerebrospinal fluid abnormalities.
•	Acute dystonia: this is usually not associated with pyrexia and autonomic instability.
•	Malignant catatonia: idiopathic malignant catatonia is due to advanced stages of psychosis and 
may be difficult to differentiate from NMS, which is also thought to be an iatrogenic malignant 
catatonia.
•	Malignant hyperthermia: this occurs after an administration of some general anaesthetic 
agents, such as potent volatile agents, e.g. halothane, suxamethonium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered a part of the collective unconscious?
questions.explanation: Jung described the collective unconscious which contains latent images of psyche development.   There are several types described. The four major types described are:  1. Persona: ‘mask’ is the outward face that we present to the world.  2. Anima and animus: unconscious mirror of gender; if we are male our animus is of unconscious   female and if we are female our animus is of unconscious male.  3. The shadow: contains more of our basic animal nature.  4. The self: the ‘archetypes of archetypes’ which unites and gives rise to oneness

questions.question_text: According to Freud's psychic apparatus, which of the following is concerned with mediating between basic desires and the judicial part of punishment?
questions.explanation: According to Freud the psychic apparatus is made up of three parts:  1. Id: basic and innate desires  2. Ego: executive part that balances the id and super-ego  3. Super-ego: concerned with punishment; the moral part

questions.question_text: Which of the following terms was first used by Thomas and Chess to refer to the harmonious interactions between a mother and her child?
questions.explanation: Goodness of fit describes the alignment between a child's temperament and parenting styles.

questions.question_text: What are phonemes referred to as?

options.text: Meaning conveyed by words and sentences
Smallest unit of sound that makes up words
The conventions about combining words according to grammatical rules
The conversational use of language in real social situations

correct_answer.text: Smallest unit of sound that makes up words

correct_answers.text: Smallest unit of sound that makes up words

questions.explanation: Phonemes are the smallest units of sound in a language that help form words.

questions.question_text: A girl starts to realise that she is a girl, which is different from being a boy. How old is she?
questions.explanation: Children typically begin to identify their gender around 2 to 3 years of age.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most appropriate combination of fears and corresponding ages?

options.text: Fear of strangers: birth to 6 months

questions.explanation: Normal fears in childhood:  0–6 months → fear of fall, loud noises, loss of support  7–12 months → fear of height, depth, strangers  1 year → fear of separation, strangers.  2–3 years → fear of the dark, animals, thunder  5–8	years	→ fear of monsters, TV creatures, ghosts  9–12 years → fear of injuries, disasters  Adolescents → fear of failure, criticism (social evaluative fears)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about developmental theories is correct? AI chose B

options.text: According to Sigmund Freud, children show interest in their peers in the phallic stage of psychosexual development
A child's ability to view the world from another's point of view represents the preoperational stage of Jean Piaget
A child who obeys the rules laid down by teachers has reached the preconventional stage 1 of Jean Piaget's theory
A child has a fear of punishment and guilt which represents Erik Erikson's autonomy vs shame stage
A child shows a gradual increase in interest in the environment and practices exploration; this represents Margaret Mahler's differentiation stage

correct_answer.text: A child who obeys the rules laid down by teachers has reached the preconventional stage 1 of Jean Piaget's theory

correct_answers.text: A child who obeys the rules laid down by teachers has reached the preconventional stage 1 of Jean Piaget's theory

questions.explanation: The preoperational stage in Piaget's theory is characterized by egocentrism, limiting the child's ability to see others' perspectives.

questions.question_text: Early life experiences can have a considerable impact on future human deviant or maladaptive behaviour. Which of the following statements about early life experiences is correct?

options.text: Psychodynamic psychiatrists rely on current data
Some affection-deprived children are capable of forming attachments
Successful adults usually come from toxic homes
Sigmund Freud postulated a unitary sequence of emotional development
The deviant or maladaptive behaviour is resistant to behavioural treatment approaches

correct_answer.text: Some affection-deprived children are capable of forming attachments

correct_answers.text: Some affection-deprived children are capable of forming attachments

questions.explanation: Research indicates that some children can form attachments despite early deprivation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding social deprivation in non-human primates is correct?

options.text: In total isolation, female primate is able to nurture the young unlike their male partners
Mother only reared primates are terrified of their mother
Peer only reared primates are clingy and timid in their reactions with others
The separation after bonding leads to stereotyped behaviour
There is an initial protest that changes to despair in partially isolated primates

correct_answer.text: Peer only reared primates are clingy and timid in their reactions with others

correct_answers.text: Peer only reared primates are clingy and timid in their reactions with others

questions.explanation: Peer-only reared primates exhibit clingy, timid behaviors during social interactions.

questions.question_text: A group of football supporters were attacked by a mob of rival supporters after a humiliating defeat of their team. They all became the 'enemy' and even innocent bystanders were attacked. Which of the following social determinants describes this behaviour?
questions.explanation: Anonymity can lead to decreased personal responsibility, resulting in aggression in crowds.

questions.question_text: What type of message would be the most persuasive communication for the more intelligent recipient?
questions.explanation: In persuasive communication, there are key aspects relating to the message and attitude change,   which include:  1. Message repetition can be a persuasive influence leading to attitude change.  2. Explicit messages are more persuasive for less intelligent recipients. 3. Implicit messages are more persuasive for more intelligent recipients.  4. Interactive personal discussions are more persuasive than mass media.  5. One-sided communications are more persuasive for those who are less intelligent and/or   already favourably disposed to the message.  6. Two-sided presentations are more effective with intelligent and neutral recipients.  7. A low-anxiety recipient is more influenced by a high-fear message, and vice versa.

questions.question_text: Which of the following experiments demonstrated the power of conformity?
questions.explanation: The Asch experiment highlighted the influence of group pressure on individual decision-making.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old unemployed man has been smoking cannabis for 4–5 years. He did not see this as a problem and said that he used it to relax him and get on with his life. He believed that his parents' worries were excessive. Which of Prochaska and DiClemente's stages of change is reflected here?
questions.explanation: In the precontemplation stage, the individual is not aware of any issues with their behavior.

questions.question_text: A 41-year-old woman completed her alcohol detoxification at home 6 months ago and has been abstinent since then. Which of Prochaska and DiClemente's stages of change is reflected here?
questions.explanation: She is in the maintenance phase, having successfully abstained and managed her behavior for 6 months.

questions.question_text: Which of the following therapies works on the basis that the current problems in the family originate from past experiences of individual members?
questions.explanation: Psychodynamic therapy focuses on how past experiences shape present behavior and family dynamics.

questions.question_text: In psychodynamic psychotherapy, exploration of transference, countertransference and resistance is discussed with a supervisor. When does this happen during the therapy?
questions.explanation: These concepts are generally addressed during the middle sessions of therapy.

questions.question_text: A 58-year-old woman was going through a divorce. Her mother had passed away 6 months ago. She became a grandmother recently. She was not coping with life and sought psychological help. Which is the most appropriate therapy for her?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal therapy is well-suited for those dealing with relationship issues and transitions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about prevention of substance misuse is correct?

options.text: Primary prevention aims to prevent the further progression of a condition by identifying and treating cases at an early stage
Primary prevention aims at reducing the prevalence of hazardous drinking or hazards of drinking
Primary prevention can be achieved by harm reduction
Secondary prevention can be achieved by controlling the availability of alcohol and drugs
Secondary prevention can be achieved by targeting the whole population

correct_answer.text: Primary prevention aims at reducing the prevalence of hazardous drinking or hazards of drinking

correct_answers.text: Primary prevention aims at reducing the prevalence of hazardous drinking or hazards of drinking

questions.explanation: Primary prevention focuses on preventing issues related to alcohol before they develop.

questions.question_text: Who was a major figure in psychiatry and neurology from 1856 to 1926 and also created the term 'dementia praecox'?
questions.explanation: Emil Kraepelin introduced the term 'dementia praecox', paving the way for modern schizophrenia classification.

questions.question_text: Which French psychiatrist from the eighteenth century used a term to describe deteriorated patients whose illness began in adolescence?
questions.explanation: Benedict Morel referred to this condition as 'dementia précoce' based on his observations.

questions.question_text: In which year did Jacob Kasanin introduce the term 'schizoaffective disorder'?
questions.explanation: Kasanin introduced the term 'schizoaffective disorder' in 1933, linking schizophrenia and mood disorders.

questions.question_text: A 26-year-old unmarried woman was unaware of her hatred towards her mother. However, she often felt inexplicably resentful towards older women in positions of authority. She could not understand why she felt like this for several years. Which of the following can explain this situation? AI chose D
questions.explanation: Projection involves attributing one's own feelings, in this case, onto others.

questions.question_text: A 49-year-old single man had been devoted to his mother but was cold and distant with his 80-year-old father. He was unaware of his sexual interest in his mother for many years and his death wish for his father. Which of the following can explain this situation?
questions.explanation: Repression pushes uncomfortable feelings about the parents out of conscious awareness.

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old male lawyer wished for his child to be a lawyer too, but unfortunately, the child died in a car accident. Since the child's death, the lawyer has started to offer free legal advice to students. Which is the most likely defence mechanism?
questions.explanation: Altruism allows the lawyer to cope with his loss by helping others through legal advice.

questions.question_text: A 29-year-old woman had an affair with her neighbour but she accused her husband of cheating on her. What is the most likely phenomenon?
questions.explanation: This scenario exemplifies projection, where her own infidelity is attributed onto her husband.

questions.question_text: In which category of the DSM-IV is schizotypal disorder classified?
questions.explanation: Schizotypal disorder is classified under personality disorders in the DSM-IV.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old male professional footballer was not able to score an easy goal in a Premier League match. Since then, he has started to think that he was not a good player. Which is the most likely cognitive distortion?
questions.explanation: Selective abstraction is when he focuses solely on one negative incident and disregards his overall abilities.

questions.question_text: Who was the first person to describe the condition currently known as schizoaffective disorder?
questions.explanation: Jacob Kasanin was the first to describe schizoaffective disorder in 1933.

questions.question_text: Who first described a condition called folie circulaire?
questions.explanation: Jules Falret originally described folie circulaire, characterizing alternating moods of depression and mania.

questions.question_text: Erikson's stages of human psychosexual development differ from those of Freud in several areas. Which of the following is one such area?

options.text: Development depends on successful negotiation of stages
Erikson's stages have both positive and negative aspects
The emphasis is on external events
They both follow the theory of infantile sexuality

questions.explanation: Erikson's theory extends across the lifespan, unlike Freud's which focuses primarily on early development.

questions.question_text: With what is Jean-Martin Charcot most credited?
questions.explanation: Jean-Martin Charcot is best known for his work in classifying neurological disorders and advancing modern neurology.

questions.question_text: According to Jean Piaget, the semiotic function in children emerges during their cognitive development. In which stage of cognitive development does this happen?
questions.explanation: The semiotic function, which refers to the ability to use symbols, appears in the preoperational stage.

questions.question_text: Which phenomenon did Margaret Mead describe in her book Coming of Age in Samoa?

options.text: An absence of adolescent turmoil such as competitiveness/aggression
The lack of tribal rivalry because they were peace loving
The low incidence of suicide among young people in the society
The Oedipus complex in Samoan societies
The passing rites/rituals of adolescent girls

correct_answer.text: An absence of adolescent turmoil such as competitiveness/aggression

correct_answers.text: An absence of adolescent turmoil such as competitiveness/aggression

questions.explanation: Mead's work suggested cultural factors led to a lack of adolescent turmoil in Samoan society.

questions.question_text: Which of the following in human beings was prompted by the work of the great ethologist Karl Von Frisch?
questions.explanation: Karl Von Frisch studied communication in bees, which influenced research in human communication systems.

questions.question_text: Which law is made by a legislative process, according to the British judicial system?
questions.explanation: Statute law is created through a formal legislative process by Parliament.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man was shocked when he looked into the mirror and did not see his reflection. What is this phenomenon called?
questions.explanation: Negative autoscopic hallucination involves not seeing one's reflection in the mirror.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old medical student was searching the literature for depression and EEG. She was interested in knowing what changes would be seen in depression. What is the most likely EEG change seen in depression? AI chose D
questions.explanation: Depression is associated with increased slow-wave sleep patterns along with changes in sleep architecture.

questions.question_text: According to Melanie Klein's theory of psychoanalysis what does the paranoid–schizoid position stand for?

options.text: Children realise that their mothers have both positive and negative aspects
An infant projects feelings of rage and hatred onto the mother and fears the same feelings from the mother
The infant splits his or her experiences into 'good' and 'bad' elements of the mother and him- or herself
The infant fears attack from the 'bad' mother
The infant has unconscious knowledge of bodily functions

correct_answer.text: The infant splits his or her experiences into 'good' and 'bad' elements of the mother and him- or herself

correct_answers.text: The infant splits his or her experiences into 'good' and 'bad' elements of the mother and him- or herself

questions.explanation: The paranoid-schizoid position describes splitting of good and bad in the infant's perception of the mother.

questions.question_text: Who propagated the person-centred theory of personality and psychotherapy?
questions.explanation: Carl Rogers created the person-centered approach emphasizing individual experiences.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychotropic drugs has high absorption of moisture when it comes into contact with moist air or humidity? AI chose C
questions.explanation: Lithium is hygroscopic and absorbs moisture; thus, it must be stored properly to maintain efficacy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Carl Jung is correct?

options.text: Jung's concept of the 'Anima' referred to the feminine qualities of a man
Jung continued to work on Freud's ideas of infantile sexuality
Jung described the concept of the collective unconscious
Jung described 'persona' as a person's true identity
Jung was influenced by antiquity and ancient Greek mythologies

correct_answers.text: Jung described the concept of the collective unconscious

questions.question_text: Who was the first person to use the terms 'mania' and 'melancholia' to describe mental illness?
questions.explanation: Hippocrates is credited with defining mania and melancholia in his work on mental health.

questions.question_text: Who is credited as the first person to describe the social origins of depression?
questions.explanation: Brown and Harris's research illustrated how social factors can lead to depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not form one of the criteria for acute intoxication of alcohol in the ICD-10?

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about lithium is correct?

Concomitant use of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors leads to decreased serum lithium levels
Concomitant use of serotonin selective reuptake inhibitors can lead to the serotonin syndrome

questions.question_text: Who said 'Is there such a thing as mental illness?' and is also known for the antipsychiatry movement?
questions.explanation: Thomas Szasz was a prominent critic of psychiatry and questioned the legitimacy of mental illness as a concept.

questions.question_text: In western Europe, which court has the highest binding power?
questions.explanation: The European Court has the highest authority, especially regarding European Union law.

questions.explanation: David et al (1995) investigated the association of left-handedness, epilepsy and hearing impairment   with schizophrenia in the cohort study of 50,000 male Swedish conscripts, linked to the Swedish   National Register of Psychiatric Care.
